target_customer: Indian retail investors holding mutual funds or shares who need cash without selling
problem: Investors needing cash take personal loans above 18% interest or liquidate investments, while loans against their holdings start near 10%.
business_model: Loan service provider earning from lending partners (Bajaj Finance, DSP Finance sanction the loans); no fee to borrower stated
product_category: Loans against mutual funds and securities

founders.name: Ashutosh Purohit
prior_employers: Navi (led mutual fund launch and growth)
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders attended the same college but does not name it.

founders.name: Aryan Agarwal
previous_startups: A capital management company in India (name and outcome not stated)

competitors.name: Tata Capital
competitors.what: Fully digital loan against mutual funds with lien marking

technical_complexity.rationale: Digital KYC, portfolio retrieval, e-mandate and e-sign integrations with depositories and lenders are integration heavy but standard.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on lending partners and AMFI registration; larger platforms later launched the same product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per Business Standard, PhonePe, Paytm, BharatPe and Cred rolled out loans against mutual funds, with PhonePe and ET Money launching in 2025.

market_need_then: The company cites 65 million Indian investors and over 30% of personal loan borrowers holding investments while paying roughly double the rate they could get; claims are the company's own.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and reassuring: The Good Loan Company, no hidden fees, no surprises

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline and trust positioning, but the name resembles Venmo and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Yenmo is an active Winter 2024 company that raised a reported $500K seed in March 2024 and a further round of about 9.2 crore rupees in 2025. It works through RBI regulated lending partners. Big platforms entered the same product in 2025, so scale depends on cost of acquiring borrowers.
notes: The first round is confirmed by Business Standard and fintech.global. The 9.2 crore rupee round (about $1.06M per CB Insights) is from Entrackr; date 2025-03 comes from CB Insights and an aggregator, and the USD amount is left null because of the currency conversion. Success factor incumbent_weakness is a loose fit (personal loans at 18%+). Founding year not found. The Tata Capital entry was dated 2021 and is an incumbent, not a startup.
